info.title: OhrTech Management API
info.description: Manage your organisation's OhrTech devices: status, settings, fleets, tasks, remote control and remote ADB. Every call takes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: either a person's access token (sign in with the device flow under /v1/auth) or a service account token (`ohrs_…`, created in the portal under Service accounts).

get.summary: The app's managed configuration: the settings its newest version declares (app_restrictions.xml)
The app's configuration in a fleet: what the fleet sets, and what its devices get

put.summary: Replace what a fleet sets in an app's configuration, and send it to the fleet's devices

delete.summary: Stop setting an app's configuration in a fleet (parent fleets' values apply)

get.summary: The app's configuration on one device: its own overrides, and what the app gets

put.summary: Replace a device's own overrides of an app's configuration, and send them

delete.summary: Remove a device's own overrides of an app's configuration (its fleet's values apply)

get.summary: Your organisations' apps, and OhrTech's catalog and platform apps

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Only apps with this package name (several apps may share one).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only apps of this kind: org, catalog or platform.

post.summary: Add an app: a package name and your name for it (several apps may share a package)

get.summary: One app, with its newest versions and fleets
An app's versions, newest first

post.summary: The request body is the APK. It must be this app's package; its version code must be newer than every version already uploaded, and it must be signed with the same key (unless allowNewSigningKey). A 409 also carries appId, packageName and versionCode, plus latestVersionCode and exists (that version code is already uploaded) or the two keys' signingKeySha256 and expectedSigningKeySha256, so a pipeline that runs again can tell its own earlier upload from a mistake.

parameters.name: allowNewSigningKey
parameters.description:
Accept an APK signed with a different key than the previous version.
            Devices refuse such an update unless the new key is a rotation (APK signature scheme v3) of the old one.

patch.summary: Hold, offer or enforce a version (and, for OhrTech's apps, its notes)

get.summary: Which devices run the enforced version, and which are still getting it
The apps a fleet's devices get

put.summary: Give an app to a fleet's devices

delete.summary: Stop giving an app to a fleet's devices: they uninstall it

get.summary: Whether a fleet gets an OhrTech app's updates automatically or only once approved

put.summary:
Manual keeps the fleet's devices on the approved version for as long as the organisation wants:
switching to manual without a version approves what the fleet gets now. Approving a version moves
the devices to it at the fleet's update timing; devices never go back to an older one.

delete.summary: Let a fleet follow its parent's policy for an OhrTech app again

get.summary: When a fleet's devices install app updates

put.summary: Set when a fleet's devices install app updates: screen off, a maintenance window, or immediately

delete.summary: Let a fleet follow its parent's update timing again

get.summary: The OhrTech Device Identity Root, PEM: trust it to check any app certificate's device

get.summary: Your organisation's issuing CAs

put.summary: Upload the CA certificate your client root issued from the CSR, with its chain

post.summary: Stop the issuing CA issuing (certificates already issued stay valid until they expire)

get.summary: An app's certificates on a fleet: its issuing CA, private CAs and imported certificates

put.summary: Give an app an issuing CA, private CAs to trust and imported client certificates (PKCS#12, sealed)

delete.summary: Stop setting the app's certificates on this fleet (a parent fleet's apply)

get.summary: The client certificates issued to the device's apps, newest first
An app's crashes, grouped: how often, on how many devices, in which versions, first and last seen
The reports of one crash, newest first: device, version, stack and the app's last log lines
The crashes of the hub's apps on one device, newest first

post.summary: Check an app key's attestation chain: which OhrTech unit made it, for which app, and whether to trust it
Stop vouching for a device (lost, retired or compromised): its attestation chains fail, and it gets no new attestation keys

get.summary: The OhrTech Attestation Root, PEM: what an offline verifier trusts
The unit attestation key certificates OhrTech no longer vouches for, by serial: a JWS signed by the OhrTech Attestation Status certificate (no sign-in)
What an app may change through the Device SDK on the fleet's devices

put.summary: Pre-approve USB devices (vendor and product id, optionally serial) and accessories (manufacturer and model) for an app

delete.summary: Stop setting the app's USB devices on this fleet (a parent fleet's apply)

get.summary: The USB devices and accessories attached to the device, as it last reported, and which apps they're approved for
What apps changed through the Device SDK, and what the Agent refused, newest first
Who the caller is, and their organisations and permissions
The devices of the caller's organisations

parameters.description: Only devices that are (true) or are not (false) online.

The apps installed on the device, as it last reported them

Sends the device a ping; it answers with a check-in (fresh status) within seconds when it is
reachable. A device on mobile data may only hear it at its next scheduled check-in.
Ask the device for one app's logs: its logcat, what it logged through the Device SDK, its recent events (a LogBundle task)

The fleets of the caller's organisations

get.summary: The device's tasks, newest first

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only tasks older than this one: pass the last taskId of the previous page.

post.summary: Create a task and send it to the device

get.summary: One task, with what the device reported

post.summary: Show a message on the device's screen (a ShowToast task)
Lift kiosk mode on the device for some minutes, without the exit PIN, or end that early (a KioskExit task)

Runs a command as adb shell would, as the shell user. It returns the task at once; the device runs it when it gets it, within seconds when online. Poll the task until it is success or failed, then read shell.

own.description: What this fleet or device sets (secrets masked).

effective.description: What the app gets here after every level above (for a fleet: its devices, before their own overrides).

problems.description: Where the effective values don't fit the app's newest schema (unknown keys, wrong types).

versionCode.description:
The version whose schema this is: the newest that declares one (null: none does,
            and any values are accepted).

restrictions.description: The app's settings, as its app_restrictions.xml declares them.

permission.description: A privileged permission one of the app's versions requests.

state.description:
granted: approved, so the app's devices get it. waiting: no approval yet; the app runs
            without it. never: OhrTech never grants it (it would let an app escalate further or escape management).

approvedFor.description:
Where the approval comes from: org (the app's organisation) or app (this OhrTech
            app); null when not granted.

mode.description:
automatic: each version OhrTech enforces. manual: only the version approved here; nothing newer
            until someone in the organisation approves it. OhrTech can't override a manual fleet.

approvedVersionCode.description:
For manual: the version the fleet's devices may run (null: none newer than what
            each device has). Devices never go back to an older version.

inheritedFromFleetId.description:
The fleet up the tree this policy comes from; null when this fleet set it, or
            nobody did (automatic).

targetVersionCode.description: What the fleet's devices get under this policy.

waiting.description: Newer versions that wait for approval (manual only), newest first.

reminders.description: For manual: the organisation is emailed weekly while a security release waits.

state.description:
held: devices don't get it. available: offered to the device, whose own app installs it
            when it is ready, through the Device SDK. enforced: every device in the app's fleets installs it.

signingKeySha256.description: SHA-256 of the signer's public key (apksigner's "public key SHA-256 digest").

permissions.description: The permissions the APK asks for.

notes.description: What OhrTech says about a catalog or platform release, such as the security fixes in it.

note.description: Why OhrTech approves it, kept with the approval.

valid.description:
The chain(s) verify to the OhrTech root, the key is in the TEE, the challenge matches, and the hub
            still vouches for the unit. Problems lists what fails OhrTech's policy (boot state, boot key, patch
            level, the package asked for): a server should accept only Valid with no Problems.

deviceId.description: The unit (dev_…). Null when its attestation key certificate predates units being named.

inYourOrganisation.description: The device is one of the caller's; only then are FleetId and the app named.

publicKeys.description: The attested keys' SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64: ec, and mlDsa65 for the hybrid suite. Pin them.

remoteControl.description: The device's Agent supports remote control.

shellCommands.description: The device can run shell commands (POST /v1/devices/{deviceId}/shell).

yourPermissions.description: What the caller may do to this device.

token.description: A LiveKit participant token; it can be used to join for 10 minutes.

signature.description: What groups the same crash (16 hex): pass it to ListCrashReports.

title.description: The exception, signal or ANR and where.

versionCodes.description: The app versions it happened in, newest first.

versionCode.description: The installed version's code; VersionHubShipped false when the APK wasn't the one the hub shipped.

report.description: The stack (Java), the backtrace (native) or the main thread (ANR), trimmed.

log.description: The app's last log lines before it.

orgId.description: The organisation; needed only when you belong to more than one.

kind.description: org (the default). catalog and platform are OhrTech's, and need OhrTech staff.

inherited.description: What the device's fleets manage, merged root first.

inheritedFrom.description: The fleet each inherited key comes from.

effective.description: What the device must follow: platform defaults, fleets, then its own overrides.

revision.description: A fingerprint of the effective policy; the device reports the one it applied.

url.description: Show it in an iframe, or open it. It carries its credential after '#': treat it like a password.

expiresAt.description: The link opens the viewer until then; a viewer that is already showing stays connected.

minutes.description:
1 to 240: how long kiosk mode is lifted (it also ends when the screen turns off). 0: back to
            kiosk mode now.

csrPem.description: Sign it with your client root (a CA certificate for the same subject and key) and upload the result.

ohrTechCertificatePem.description: OhrTech's certificate for it, and OhrTechChainPem up to the OhrTech Device Identity Root.

orgCertificatePem.description: Your root's certificate for it, once uploaded.

KeyAttestationDto.description: A key attestation as the app got it from OhrKeys.attest (byte fields base64), and the challenge you issued.

KeyAttestationVerdictDto.description:
Whether the key was made in this device's TEE for that app, bound to that challenge.
Reason says why not; AppId and PackageName are the app it belongs to.

status.description: pending, running, success or failed (the task's).

downloadUrl.description: Where to download the zip, for an hour (DownloadExpiresAt); null until it is uploaded.

kind.description:
org: your organisation's own app. catalog: provided by OhrTech; add it to your fleets.
            platform: part of the OS on every device, such as Vanadium System WebView; updated where the OS has it.
            OhrTech releases the versions of catalog and platform apps; each fleet chooses Automatic or Manual
            (GET /v1/fleets/{fleetId}/apps/{appId}/policy).

orgId.description: The organisation the app belongs to; null for catalog and platform apps.

enforcedVersionCode.description:
The version the app's fleets install: the newest enforced one (for a
            catalog or platform app, what Automatic fleets get).

fleets.description: The fleets whose devices get the app (your fleets, for a catalog app; none for a platform app).

userId.description: The person (usr_…); null for a service account.

serviceAccountId.description: The service account (sa_…); null for a person.

orgs.description:
The caller's organisations, each with every permission the caller holds there (a person holds the
            device permissions through membership alone).

fleetId.description: The fleet to move the device to, or null for none. Required, so that a missing value never moves it.

consent.description: unattended, notify or confirm. Only stricter than the device's setting takes effect.

takeOver.description: End another open session on this device first (default false).

embedOrigins.description: Web origins (https://app.example.com) that may show the viewer page in an iframe. At most 5. A service account limited to some sites may name only those; naming none then means all of them.

fingerprint.description: The Foundation OS build fingerprint, as last reported.

buildDate.description: When that build was made, as last reported.

securityPatch.description: The Android security patch level the device runs (YYYY-MM-DD), as last reported. Null until the device reports it.

attached.description:
As the device reported it: {"vendorId", "productId", "manufacturer", "product", "serial", "approvedFor": [package]}
            for devices, {"accessory": true, "manufacturer", "model", ...} for accessories.

note.description: What OhrTech said when approving it.

PolicyDto.description: Settings by key, each with how it is managed and the value to apply.

PolicyPatchDto.description: For PATCH: a key set to null stops overriding it on this device.

message.description: The sealed, signed envelope, base64 (PushSealer, or docs/push.md §2).

priority.description: "normal" (default) or "high": wakes the device from Doze and lets the app start a foreground service.

ttl.description: Seconds the hub keeps trying, 1 to 2,419,200 (28 days); default 86,400.

collapseKey.description: A message still on its way with the same token and key is replaced.

PushResult.description: Per message, in order: its id (pmsg_…), or why it was refused.

reapply.description: Set settings to apply again now, overwriting what the person at the device changed them to.

status.description: queued, sent, delivered, dropped, expired or replaced.

policyConsent.description: The consent the device's own settings require.

status.description: pending, notified, awaiting_consent, active, closed, denied, failed.

consent.description: unattended, notify or confirm: what the device was told to do.

inSync.description: The device applied the current revision.

allowMobileData.description: Upload on mobile data too; otherwise the device waits for Wi-Fi (up to a day).

installedVersionCode.description:
The version of this app the device runs; null if it has none, or has
            the package as another app (a flavour it no longer gets, uninstalled before this one goes on).

targetVersionCode.description:
The version this device should run: the newest enforced one, or for a catalog or
            platform app on a Manual fleet, the version its organisation approved (null: none).

policy.description: For a catalog or platform app: automatic or manual, its fleet's choice; null for an org app.

detail.description:
Why it failed, as the device reported it; what a waiting device waits for; for a pending
            device that has the package as another app, which one.

targetVersionCode.description: The newest enforced version: what devices install, unless their fleet is Manual.

command.description: What to run, as with adb shell: sh -c runs it, so pipes, ; and && work. At most 4000 characters.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long it may run, 1 to 600 seconds (default 60). Then it is stopped and the task fails.

expiresAt.description: Don't run it if the device gets it after this time, for example because it was offline. Default: whenever it gets it.

areas.description: What the app may change on this fleet's devices: this fleet's grant, or the nearest parent fleet's.

own.description: This fleet's own grant, or null when it inherits one (or none).

inheritedFrom.description: The fleet whose grant applies when this fleet has none of its own.

alwaysAllowed.description: What every app the hub installs may do without a grant.

fleetIds.description: The fleets it may act on, each with every fleet below it; null for the whole organisation.

deviceIds.description: Devices it may act on outside those fleets.

embedOrigins.description: The only web origins its remote control sessions may be embedded in; null for any.

issuingCaId.description: The organisation's issuing CA for the app's device-made keys; null: none.

trust.description: Private CAs (PEM) the app trusts besides the system's.

imported.description: Client certificates from your PKI: {"alias", "pkcs12" (base64), "password"}; "*" keeps a stored one.

values.description:
The keys to set (null unsets one: the app's default applies, whatever a parent set).
            Secrets as {"$secret": "…"}; {"$secret": "*"} keeps the stored one.

approvedVersionCode.description: For manual: the version to approve; omitted, the version the fleet gets now.

reminders.description: Email weekly reminders while a security release waits (default true); null leaves it.

state.description: held, available or enforced; null leaves it.

notes.description: For a catalog or platform app (OhrTech staff): what the release changes; null leaves it.

security.description: For a catalog or platform app (OhrTech staff): the release fixes security vulnerabilities.

areas.description: Areas from the settings catalogue's sdk.access options. Empty takes away what a parent fleet grants.

devices.description:
Each {"vendorId", "productId", "serial"?, "name"?} (ids 0-65535 or hex "0x05e0") or {"manufacturer", "model", "name"?}.
            Empty takes away what a parent fleet approves.

revision.description: The policy the device must follow, as a fingerprint.

appliedRevision.description: What the device last reported applying.

exitCode.description: The command's exit status; null if it did not finish (it timed out, or could not start: see error).

stdout.description: Its standard output: the first 64 KiB.

stderr.description: Its standard error: the first 64 KiB.

truncated.description: There was more output than that.

timedOut.description: It ran out of time and was stopped.

error.description: Why it did not run, when it did not.

status.description: pending, running, success, failed or cancelled.

result.description: What the device reported when it finished, as JSON (for a shell command, see shell).

messages.description: What the device reported while running it, oldest first.

createdBy.description: Who created it through the API or the portal; null for the tasks OhrTech creates (updates).

inheritedFromFleetId.description:
The fleet up the tree this timing comes from; null when this fleet set it or
            nobody did (screen_off).

description.description: In words, such as "every day 02:00–05:00, or when the screen is off".

mode.description:
screen_off: once nobody has used the device for 2 minutes. window: only inside the window, even
            in use. window_or_screen_off: either. immediate: at once, even mid-use. Only updates wait: an app the device
            doesn't have yet (just assigned to the fleet, or a device new to the fleet) always installs at once.

days.description: Days the window opens, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday); empty or null: every day.

start.description: Window start, HH:mm, the device's local time.

end.description: Window end, HH:mm; earlier than start, it runs past midnight.

certificatePem.description: The CA certificate your client root issued from the CSR.

chainPem.description: Its issuers up to and including your self-signed root.

devices.description: What applies on the fleet: its own entries, or the nearest parent fleet's.

own.description: This fleet's own entries; null when it inherits (InheritedFrom).

challenge.description: The server's challenge the app attested with, base64.

ec.description: The EC key's chain, base64 DER, the key's certificate first.

mlDsa65.description: For the ec-mldsa65 suite, the ML-DSA-65 key's chain. Both must pass.

package.description: The package the key must belong to, if the server wants it checked.

signerSha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the app's signing certificate (hex), if the server wants it checked: a
            Problem unless one of the app's signers matches. Without it, compare `signerSha256` in the answer yourself.

versionCode.description: A version newer than what the fleet gets, waiting for approval.

bearer.description: A person's access token from /v1/auth/token, or a service account token (ohrs_…).
